slides.title: Welcome to the Children's Constitution Club!
slides.tip: Play welcome music.

slides.title: Roleplay Activity
body: Do you or your family follow the news?
Where do they get their news from — TV, newspapers, WhatsApp, or YouTube?
Let's understand through a roleplay how the same news is told differently on different platforms like TV, community meetings, email, WhatsApp etc.
We need 5 students for the roleplay!
Those who are interested in acting
Those who can read clearly so everyone can hear
slides.tip: Ask for volunteers who are enthusiastic and can read clearly.

slides.title: Roleplay — Assign Roles
body: Cut the sheet and give one slip to each of the 5 students:
Student 1: Narrator
Student 2: TV Journalist
Student 3: Local Leader
Student 4: Residents' Welfare Association & Parents
Student 5: Social Media & WhatsApp Champions
I need 3 students to play the role of the "Public". You 3 will need to step outside the classroom, and I will call you when it's your turn.
slides.tip: Give each volunteer their slip from Annexure 1. Select 3 'public' volunteers and send them outside.

slides.title: Roleplay — Preparation
slides.brief: The five volunteers should read their slips 2-3 times to prepare. Get ready to read a bit dramatically!
slides.tip: 1 minute preparation time.

slides.title: Roleplay — Reading Time!
body: Are the five volunteers ready to read?
Let's start in order from Student 1 to Student 4.
slides.tip: Students 1-4 read in order. Student 5 must NOT read yet.

slides.title: Invite the Public + Student 5
body: Now let's invite the public back into the classroom! Welcome back!
Now WhatsApp Champions (Student 5) will read the last slip, and the public must listen carefully.
slides.tip: Call the 3 public volunteers back into the classroom.

slides.title: Questions for the Public
body: The public must answer:
questions: What did you understand from the WhatsApp message you just heard?
slides.tip: Only the students playing the 'public' role should answer.

slides.title: The Narrator Reads Again
body: Now let's call the narrator back! Narrator, can you read your slip once more — this time for the public?
Did you understand what the narrator said? Was it different from what Student 5 (Social Media / WhatsApp Champion) read?
slides.tip: Ask the public: did you notice the difference between the narrator's and Student 5's versions?

slides.title: Class Discussion
body: What happened in this example?
Why did the original news change depending on who was telling it?
What are the consequences of spreading fake news or giving wrong information?
Now that you have heard all versions of the news — how did you finally decide what was true?
Did you believe everything immediately?
Did you pause and think?
Did you ask questions or compare what different people said?
slides.tip: Show questions one after the other. Let students reach conclusions themselves.

slides.title: Scientific Temper — What Skill Is This?
slides.tip: Play MC video. Wait for students to guess.
kn_script: When we ask questions, verify facts, and think before believing or sharing something — we are using a very important skill.
Can you guess what that skill is called?

slides.tip: Reveal the answer after students guess.
body: The answer is: Scientific Temper!
Asking for evidence
Thinking calmly
Being open to verifying the truth
Not making decisions based only on emotions
This protects us from fake news and misinformation, and helps us become alert, aware, and informed citizens.
Scientific Temper = Thinking like a detective!

slides.title: 4W Test
body: Before believing or sharing any information — ask the 4Ws!
4W Test — Sequential Interaction
① WHO? — Who is saying this? Who is telling the information about the person from another state? Options: News channels, Secretary, Others
② WHERE? — Where can I cross-check this information? Options: Internet, Various news channels, Newspapers, Government websites

③ WHAT DO I THINK? — What is my perspective? What did I feel about this topic from the beginning? Reflection: Did I accept this report just because of my personal feeling that 'outsiders are always troublemakers'?
④ WILL I CHANGE? — Am I ready to change my previously held perspective based on new evidence?
slides.tip: Walk through each W step by step. Let students respond to each before moving to the next.

slides.title: What are the 4Ws?
body: The 4Ws is a simple and useful tool to help you determine whether the news or information you receive is true or false!
Stop once — ask yourself 4 questions:
WHO? — Who is saying this?
WHERE? — Where can I cross-check this information?
WHAT DO I THINK? — What is my perspective on this?
WILL I CHANGE? — Will I change my perspective if I get new evidence?
Use the 4Ws — think and verify before you believe!
Now let's see another example!
slides.tip: Write 4Ws on the board: WHO, WHERE, WHAT DO I THINK, WILL I CHANGE.

slides.title: Social Media Post
body: Imagine…
You saw this post this morning.
BREAKING NEWS: Government announces ban on online transactions nationwide!

In a shocking move, the Indian government has reportedly decided to ban all types of online payments from next month, citing rising cybersecurity threats. According to a leaked government notification circulating on social media, popular platforms such as UPI, net banking, and digital wallets will be completely shut down in phases to protect citizens from increasing cyber fraud. The directive has warned businesses and individuals to prepare for cash-based transactions, causing widespread concern among digital economy stakeholders.

Financial experts fear this sudden decision could cripple businesses dependent on digital payments, while citizens are rushing to ATMs and banks to withdraw cash. Several e-commerce websites have reportedly started revising their payment systems, while fintech companies are scrambling to get clarity from government sources.
slides.tip: Ask a volunteer to read the post aloud.

slides.title: Social Media Influencer
body: This news is being widely shared on Social Media Influencers, WhatsApp Forwards, Twitter/X and Facebook.
Another thing…
Your favourite Influencer whom you always follow has also shared this.
What will you do?
slides.tip: Let students discuss what they would do.

slides.title: Apply the 4W Test
body: Let's apply the 4W Test to this social media post!
slides.tip: Walk through the 4W application with the UPI ban example.

slides.title: How Does Fake News Spread?
body: Fake news spreads through gossip, influence, and hearsay.
slides.tip: Discuss the three ways fake news spreads.

slides.title: AI Makes Lies Look Real
body: AI (Artificial Intelligence) can create fake images, fake videos, and fake quotes that deceive people!
This makes it even more important to always stop and verify before believing or sharing anything.
slides.tip: Show AI-generated fake news examples.

slides.title: Constitution Connection
body: Which constitutional value from the Preamble best fits the activities and discussions we did today?
slides.tip: Show Preamble images. Accept all responses.

slides.title: Constitution Connection — Quiz
body: Think and answer!
According to Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, which quality is it a citizen's duty to develop?
A. Secularism
B. Democratic values
C. Scientific temper
D. Civic responsibility
Select your answer!
✅ Correct answer: C. Scientific temper
Article 51A(h): It is the Fundamental Duty of every citizen to develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
slides.tip: Let students guess before revealing the answer.

slides.title: Fundamental Duty
slides.tip: Play MC video.
kn_script: Our Constitution guarantees us rights. There is a Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution about verifying the truth of what we read, hear, and speak, and thinking critically.
Can you guess what this Fundamental Duty actually says?
Yes! It is: to develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
Did you know that applying the 4Ws test is part of our Fundamental Duty?

slides.title: Your 4W Challenge — Ripple Task
body: After you go home…
📱 With your parents' permission, pick any Forwarded Message / Online News from their mobile.
Use the 4W Test to verify it!
What to do next?
Discuss with your parents and share the experience of one Forwarded Message / Online News you verified in the next session.
🌊 This is your "Ripple of Change"! Write your experience and put it in the Change Champion Box.
📄 Use the handout: The handout provided will help you verify information, data, and news.
slides.tip: Distribute Annexure 3 (4Ws handout) to all students.

slides.title: Let's Come Together for Change!
body: We are now part of a new journey…
Let's learn from each other
Let's use each other's strengths and talents
Let's think critically
Let's bring change together
Look at your Project Card!
Each group will receive a Project Card.
1. Read — Read the instructions on your Project Card completely.
2. Work together — Complete the activities given in the card as a group.
3. Use your time — Work on the project activities during your free time.
4. Complete in 3 weeks — Finish all given activities.
5. Have doubts? — Contact your mentors.
slides.tip: Distribute Project Cards to each group.
